Specification: Solid Shaft Diameter Design from Angle-of-Twist Limit

Use small-deformation, linear-elastic, isotropic, homogeneous torsion theory for a solid circular shaft with no coupling to bending or axial load.

Assume the given torque is uniformly distributed along the shaft length and is applied purely as torsion (no transverse shear superposed on the twist equation, since the torsional rigidity JG governs the angle-of-twist response).

Use the standard linear-elastic torsion relation for a solid circular shaft: φ = TL / (JG), where J = π d^4 / 32, so φ = 32TL / (π G d^4).

Apply the design inequality: φ ≤ φ_allow, i.e., 32TL / (π G d^4) ≤ φ_allow.

Solve for the minimum required diameter: d ≥ [32TL / (π G φ_allow)]^(1/4).

Use the following numerical inputs exactly as stated: applied torque T = 1,000,000 N·mm (1 kN·m), shaft length L = 1500 mm, enablement angle φ_allow = 0.75° total twist over the full length, convert φ_allow to radians as φ_allow = 0.75 × π / 180 ≈ 0.0130899 rad, shaft material 6061-T6 aluminum with shear modulus G = 25,939.8 MPa (≈ 25.94 GPa), keep all units consistent in N, mm, MPa.

Compute the required diameter: d_min = [32 × 1,000,000 × 1500 / (π × 25,939.8 × 0.0130899)]^(1/4) mm ≈ [4.4998 × 10^7]^(1/4) mm ≈ 81.9 mm.

Select a standard shaft diameter d ≥ 82 mm (round up to the next preferred size, e.g., 85 mm, to provide margin over the exact minimum).

Verify the design by back-substituting the chosen d into φ = 32TL / (π G d^4) and confirm that φ ≤ 0.75°.

Report the final response quantities explicitly: required minimum diameter d_min ≈ 81.9 mm, recommended design diameter d = 85 mm, resulting total angle of twist φ ≈ 0.75° × (81.9 / 85)^4 ≈ 0.637° at the chosen diameter, and the corresponding polar moment of inertia J = π d^4 / 32.
